topic_theme: U.S. Senate Bans Itself from Using Prediction Markets
primary_headline: US Senate Bans Members, Staff from Prediction Markets
combined_key_facts: The US Senate unanimously approved a rule-change resolution banning senators and their staff from placing bets on prediction markets.
Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio authored/introduced the 14-line resolution.
Moreno stated that engaging in prediction markets could risk monetizing the job using inside information, deteriorating constituent confidence.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer threw support behind the move, calling it a 'no-brainer' preventing Congress from turning into a casino.
The resolution came in the wake of controversies, including a special forces soldier charged with using classified info to make Polymarket bets.
Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson intends to introduce a similar resolution for the House.
Polymarket and Kalshi leadership supported the resolution, asserting it aligns with their own internal bans on insider trading.
aggregated_raw_content: Acting on a simple, 14-line resolution pushed by Ohio Republican Senator Bernie Moreno, the Senate agreed unanimously to put a restriction between members and the increasingly popular, controversial betting platforms that have drawn scrutiny over insider-trading activity and fights over who has regulatory jurisdiction. “United States Senators have no business engaging in speculative activities like prediction markets while collecting a taxpayer-funded paycheck, period,” said Senator Moreno. The US Senate on Thursday unanimously approved a resolution banning its members and staff, who are often exposed to sensitive information, from using prediction markets. The resolution, passed by unanimous consent, changed the Senate's rules and took immediate effect. “Engaging in any way in a prediction market or trying to place bets where we might have inside information deteriorates the confidence that our constituents have in us,” Republican Senator Bernie Moreno, who introduced the resolution, said on the Senate floor. “By changing the standing rules of the Senate, what we’re doing is allowing our constituents to know, once and for all, that no member of the United States Senate, no member of the staff of the United States Senate, can ever use that inside information as a way to monetize this job whatsoever,” he added. The resolution comes after a special forces soldier involved in the plan to capture former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro was charged last week, on April 23, with using classified information to make bets on Polymarket, as lawmakers also air concerns over well-timed bets on the Iran war. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on the Senate floor that “of all the issues we debate in Washington, this falls clearly in the category of a ‘no-brainer.’” “We must never allow Congress to turn into a casino where members representing the public can gamble on wars, or economic crises, or elections,” he said. “We should go further; this is a good start, but not enough,” Schumer said. “The administration and its employees must apply these very same rules too, particularly this administration, which shows such a troubling affinity to corruption and self-dealing.” Republican Representative Ashley Hinson posted to X that she would introduce a similar resolution to ban the use of prediction markets in the House. Polymarket posted on X that it fully supported the Senate resolution and its terms of service “already prohibit such conduct, but codifying this into law is a step forward for the industry.” Tarek Mansour, co-founder and CEO of rival prediction market platform Kalshi, also celebrated the resolution in a post on X, adding that it “already proactively blocks members of Congress and enforces against insider trading.”
